newsitem.title: UK: Commercial Union shares advance on results.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Union shares advance on results.

text.p: Shares in general and life insurer Commercial Union rose on Wednesday after third quarter operating profits fell on weather claims, but still managed to beat most analysts' forecasts.
The shares were up 8p at 647p by 1054 GMT after the company's nine-month operating earnings fell to 348 million stg from 384 million stg a year earlier.
"We were impressed by the very low interest charges after reducing borrowings and the underwriting performance in France," said Tony Kay, Panmure Gordon's specialist salesman.

Kay added that he may consider raising his annual forecast by around 20 million stg but would wait until after the analysts meeting and clarification over how the company is planning to classify an expected 30 million stg equalisation reserve charge.
"All things being equal I would have raised my estimate, but how the charge is to be classified could change my mind," he said.
Analysts said the differential between Commercial Union and General Accident's share price was currently too large and today's results highlighted that Commercial Union shares were undervalued.
"The shares are too cheap at their current price," Kay said. "They should be up around 685p in my opinion," he added.
